Book correction: The answer key (its item 2, which belongs to Question 1) lists (iv) under "Homogeneous". This is wrong: e^{x - y} = e^x \cdot e^{-y} is a product g(x)h(y), so (iv) is separable, and it is not homogeneous.

Book correction: The answer key prints "Separable: (i), (ii), (v), (vi) Homogeneous: (iii), (iv), (vii)". The question has only six parts, so there is no (vii), and two parts are misclassified: (iv) is separable and (vi) is homogeneous (\ln x - \ln y = -\ln\frac{y}{x}). Correct: separable (i), (ii), (iv), (v); homogeneous (iii), (vi).
